FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #3
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Oral Expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.

2. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.

3. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

4. When practising Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Comprehension.

5. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. livre
   B. porte
   C. fenêtre
   D. chaise

6. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

7. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good night only
   B. Thank you
   C. Excuse me
   D. Good morning / hello

8. When practising Grammar, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar.

9. When practising Reading for Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Vocabulary.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
10. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

11. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.

5. A — livre

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

7. D — Good morning / hello

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Vocabulary.
